newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BARCO A "SELL" SAYS BELGIAN ANALYST.
newsitem.headline: BARCO A "SELL" SAYS BELGIAN ANALYST.

text.p: Disappointing prospects for future earnings growth at Belgian electronics firm Barco NV has led Belgian broker Bank Degroof to revise downwards its recommendation on the stock.
"Our long-term scenario is revised downwards, resulting in solid overvaluation at present levels," said Degroof's Jan Longeval in a research note.
"Because we believe that earnings growth rates of between 10 and 15 percent will be a disappointment to many investors we change our recommendation from hold to sell," said Longeval.
He said Barco had forecast 1997 net current profit rise of only 10 to 15 percent, lower than the consensus forecast of more than 20 percent.

"Beyond 1997, Barco's earnings growth will undergo a significant negative impact as operating margin improvement potential is exhausted and the tax charge rises sharply from below 20 to more than 30 percent," Longeval said.
Barco last week posted a 37 percent rise in first-half consolidated net profit to 1.13 billion francs and said it expected full-year current profit to be up 25 percent.
